acceptanceCriteria: Document exact token-boundary rules with working space-separated Go case annotations and normalized selector examples.
A refusal for an adjoining-hyphen annotation explains why the matching substring is not an exact requirement token, without admitting ambiguous IDs.
Focused tests retain rejection for ambiguous ID tokens and successful linkage for a separated exact ID; preserve existing wire/matcher semantics unless separately accepted.
body: Observed workflow friction, not a confirmed Core correctness bug. Intake #391 closeout on Core 1.0.0-rc.1 build163 and Tasks build202 dev20260929.2: assertion-bearing literal t.Run("CVI-V0-002-strict-grammar", ...) selected with the documented normalized case fragment was refused claim-obligation-mismatch (claim anchor lacks the exact obligation ID). The same assertions with literal t.Run("CVI-V0-002 strict grammar", ...) linked successfully; all seven CVI requirements then linked and frozen tests passed at c429c317f2e41db7134e655439de06b67b77fd31. Hyphen adjacent to an exact requirement ID remains part of the token under containsExactRequirement, but current refusal does not identify that boundary or suggest a separator. Expected guidance/diagnostics explain exact-token matching and give a concrete space-separated annotation example without weakening the matcher. Evidence: /tmp/containment391-change-anchor-refusal.log, /tmp/containment391-ocm-links.tsv, buildlog docs/build-log/2026-09-30-workflow-intake.md; raw-selector refusal separately retained in /tmp/containment391-change-selector-refusal.log. Searches agent-memory hyphen, requirement annotation and delimiter returned none; claim-obligation-mismatch found V1-0482, which records absent requirement anchors in LSP evidence and does not cover adjoining-hyphen guidance. No source fix in this intake slice.
title: OCM: explain requirement anchor token boundaries in guidance and refusals
